Alex / Vanessa —

I've started a redline and flagged a few priority items in the attached doc (Redline_Notes_KP_20260912.docx). Summary of the top points:

1) Data processing & subprocessor clause — need to confirm whether SaaSify requires us to accept subprocessor flow-downs beyond our standard list. If yes, please provide the list of specific subprocessors you require.

2) Indemnity and limitation of liability — your draft has a mutual indemnity bucket; request clarification on whether SaaSify expects additional carve-outs for third-party IP claims tied to customer data.

3) Security evidence — we can provide a SOC 2 summary (latest assessment 2026-05) and an ISO attestation on request. Please confirm if redaction is needed before sharing.

4) Order Form: exhibit A (usage tiers) — Marissa, I left inline questions about anticipated monthly token volumes so we can confirm the right tier and reserve window.

I've attached my redline. If you can answer the subprocessor and SOC questions, I can finalize the legal pass. I'm available for a 30-minute call tomorrow morning PST if that's useful.

Attachments: Redline_Notes_KP_20260912.docx (docx)

Thanks, Kimberly — this is helpful. Quick responses inline: 

- Subprocessors: we can accept the standard list but need to ensure AWS US-WEST is included in residency and that the following partner is explicitly allowed as a subprocessor: InsightCaching LLC (caching layer).
- SOC 2: we only need the SOC 2 Type II summary and confirmation of the assessment date (2026-05 is fine). Redaction is OK for internal contact emails.
- Indemnity: we prefer mutual indemnity with a carve-out for gross negligence; we can accept Redwood's standard cap if you add a narrow IP carve-out for customer-originated code.
- Party details for signatory: SaaSify Inc., a Delaware C-corp; Billing contact: Laura Meyers <laura.meyers@saasify.com>; Tech contact: Priya Rao <priya.rao@saasify.com>; Region: us-west-2
